text.overview: The standard route on this spire and its easiest line to the top, though awkward for reaching the SE Spire. Ascend the snowy finger to reach rock, then take two pitches, fourth class into low fifth, directly to the saddle (rappel anchor atop each). A ledge line on the left may be easier but often seems wet and slimy. Beyond the saddle, follow the NE ridge on foot, with some exposed scrambling at class 3-4, then drop into a class 4 chute short of the summit and walk to the foot of the last pitch.

text.overview: Ossa Mountain is climbed by its east ridge, a long day from the Squamish side with steep forest, meadows and creek crossings below a route-finding scramble. Near the top the route downclimbs into a notch and works through a chimney section before the summit.
text.descent: Return the same way; the downclimbs and loose ground make the descent as serious as the ascent.
